How We Raise Our Beef 
Our Holistic Approach To Farming
Humane Care

Our cattle roam freely on open pastures, living stress-free lives in their natural environment with plenty of space to graze and socialize.

Regenerative Practices

We use rotational grazing and sustainable farming methods that improve soil health, sequester carbon, and enhance biodiversity.

Fresh, flash-frozen beef delivered directly to your home with convenient scheduling and eco-friendly packaging.

How are we different?

Our beef is fresher than what you'll find in the grocery store. In the store the product has passed through 6 to 8 different hands before landing on the shelf. Less hands, less time, fresher, better beef. And, you can trust that it was raised by us on our farm in the most humane way.

Our Story
Three Generations, One Mission: Premium Beef, Land Regeneration, and Community Roots
Premium Beef

Pasture-raised herds delivering rich taste you can trust

Land Regeneration

Rotational grazing and no-till cover crops rebuild living soil

Community Roots

Built on family labor, shared meals, and regional pride

About The Owners

Matt and Anna didn’t only set out to “launch a brand”; they came home. After a period in Oakland, California, they returned to Georgia with their son  Levon, to the land Anna’s grandfather (Woody) stewarded. His philosophy was straightforward: work with the farm’s natural rhythms. Matt and Anna are renewing that legacy, blending modern regenerative practices, careful pasture management, and full transparency from soil to stocking. Every decision they make honors that balance of heritage and forward thinking.

Our Practices
Grass & Grain Options

100% grass-fed and grass-finished option offerings

No-Till Planting

Preserving soil structure and microbial life

Rotational Grazing

Moving cattle regularly for optimal pasture health

Learn More
A bit of History
Charles "Woody" Schmoe purchased Blackwater Plantation in 1954.
The original rotational path for the cattle surrounded the black water swamp giving the cattle a place to cool off in the heat.
Since Anna’s generation, the swamp has served as a safe haven for wood storks.
Woody was one of a handful of contributors who supported Winn Dixie’s early beef program. "The Beef People"

Woody’s simple but profound stewardship—letting the land guide the cattle—echoes through every choice Matt and Anna make today, reminding us that true regeneration starts with respect for nature’s rhythms.  Thank you for being a part of that story.

When your regular farmers market closes for the season, you can still order Blackwater beef online and pickup at one of our scheduled Atlanta pickup locations. Select Local Pickup at checkout, choose your preferred location, available date, and place your order at least 24 hours before pickup.
